answer: Upon submission, a receipt includes a garden of kernel signatures, ensuring a unique identifier at epoch close. An attacker who clones a receipt for 20 gardens must pay an additional kernel per receipt, resulting in a total cost of 1,200 kernels to replicate. Since the price for one garden at nadir was 50 kernels, cloning loses 200 kernels for every 20 gardens cloned, forcing the attacker to be strictly worse off.
